parole.significato: To perform a kind of lively dance with hand movements.
parole.testo: From Kongo dyengula (“to gyrate the waist while dancing”), possibly from French dégringoler (“to fall down, tumble”).
Borrowed from Kongo zumbi (“fetish”). Doublet of zombie.

parole.significato: A jequirity bean, the seed of the jequirity plant (Abrus precatorius) used in beadwork or making percussion instruments.
parole.testo: From jumbie + bead. Jumbie is apparently from Kongo zumbi (“fetish, spirit”) or Kimbundu nzumbi (“god”). Compare zombie.

parole.significato: A spirit, or an object inhabited by a spirit, in Bantu religious beliefs.
A former (1967–1993) monetary unit of Zaire, one hundredth of a likuta, and one ten-thousandth of a zaire; it was issue…
parole.testo: PIE word  *pénkʷe Borrowed from Kongo sengi, senki, from French cinq (“five”) (in the sense of five sous). Doublet of cinque, fin (“five currency units”), finnuf, five, pimp (“five”), ponzu, and punch (“beverage”).

parole.significato: A carnival performer in the Caribbean who walks or dances on stilts.
parole.testo: Possibly from Kongo moko (“curer, diviner”) or from Moko, the name of a person or group of people, with English jumbie, itself from Kongo zumbi (“fetish, spirit”).
